request: a bento box-inspired collapsible UI menu component for a fictional coffee company site
thesis: A navigation menu that folds shut to one pill and opens into a Japanese bento lunchbox: compartments of different sizes, each holding one small useful thing, packed edge to edge with even gutters.
job: see the closed menu trigger in the site header and know it opens
open it (click, Enter, Space) and watch compartments unfold
scan the compartments and find where to go: beans, subscribe, brew guides, cafes, wholesale, story
act inside a compartment without leaving: pick a roast, grind, add to bag, change subscription cadence
expand one compartment further (nested collapse) to see more, collapse it again
see state change: bag count, selected roast, chosen cadence, favourites
close it (button, Escape, click outside) and get focus back to the trigger
use it on a phone: stacked 2-column grid, thumb reachable
use it with keyboard and screen reader; reduced motion respected

principles: state must be visible where the action happened
every control has a distinct hover, focus, pressed, selected state
steps: define states: closed, open, tile-expanded, selected
wire a single state object and render from it
tricks: grid-template-rows 0fr to 1fr animates height without measuring
stagger tile entrance by index with a CSS variable
use inert on hidden panel so tab order skips it
aria-live polite region for bag count
tests: tab through whole thing with no mouse
open, change three things, close, reopen: does state persist
click every tile: does anything happen

principles: varied tile spans on a shared grid
one hero tile, a few mediums, several smalls
no empty holes: spans must sum to full rows
steps: use grid-auto-flow: dense only if needed
tricks: container-ish breakpoint via media query on panel width
tests: squint: do tiles tile with no gaps

principles: type scale with a serif display voice and a sans UI voice
steps: accent only on selected and primary
tricks: inset 1px highlight plus soft outer shadow reads as lacquer
tiny uppercase label over big word
emoji-free inline SVG or CSS shapes for icons

principles: ease-out for entering, short for exits

expectations: looks like a coffee brand not a SaaS

kinds.name: dropdown bento panel from header pill
kinds.what: classic: pill trigger, panel of mixed-size tiles beneath

descriptions: fictional: Ember & Oak Coffee Roasters, small-batch, est. 2014
voice: warm, plain, a little dry humour

tokens.names: Ember & Oak, Ashgrove Roasters, Little Kettle Co.

descriptions: cream page, espresso ink, one terracotta accent, sage as secondary
no web fonts: Georgia / Iowan Old Style / Palatino stack for display; system-ui for UI

behaviors: click tile header toggles its extra content
choose roast chip: selected state shows in tile and in bag line
add to bag increments count and flashes
cadence segmented control updates price line

descriptions: short labels, real prices ($16-$22 per 12 oz), real hours

anti_keywords.not: generic hamburger dropdown list of links
anti_keywords.instead: compartments of unequal size each holding something live
warm paper cream, espresso ink, one terracotta accent

anti_keywords.not: tiles that are all identical squares
anti_keywords.instead: one hero, mediums, smalls, spans summing to full rows
inline SVG/CSS shapes, no remote images

anti_keywords.not: heavy drop shadows and glass blur
anti_keywords.instead: flat lacquer tiles with inset highlight and soft shadow
grid-rows 0fr/1fr unfold plus staggered tile entrance

checks: tab through with keyboard only; focus ring visible everywhere
open, add to bag twice, count reads 2, close, reopen: still 2
Escape closes and focus returns to trigger
360px wide: no horizontal scroll, tiles fill rows without holes
no network requests, no console errors
toggle spam 10x: ends in consistent state
built: dropdown bento panel from header pill
